Semantic fidelity is good for the safety task: top_breach is the only route to the non-accepting trap u2 and carries a dominant -10 penalty from both u0 and u1, while u0 and u1 (no top breach yet) are accepting, so task success corresponds exactly to staying in accepting states until the 300-step cut; no regression transitions are needed because a top breach is permanent and success is binary. Ordered transition coverage is complete and deterministic in every state: in u0 top_breach is matched before the kill guard, and since the environment guarantees zombie_killed and top_breach never co-occur (and likewise plant_trampled), the !top_breach conjunct is redundant but harmless; the per-state else self-loops absorb side_breach, plant_trampled and later zombie_killed, which correctly leaves side-lane breaches and trampled plants unpunished because this task concerns only the top lane. Reward safety holds: the only positive shaping is a single bounded 0.1 for the first kill against -10 for a breach, and because any breach-free policy must kill at least one zombie (top-lane zombies always get through unless killed), the bonus cannot change the set of successful policies. Minor, non-blocking notes: the kill bonus is one-shot, so once in u1 the RM gives no per-kill signal (later kills earn only the environment's own +1); a small per-kill bonus on the u1 self-loop would be a denser progress signal while remaining bounded (at most ~37 kills per episode). The u2 else self-loop absorbs repeated top_breach events without extra penalty, which is acceptable given the binary success condition.
